title: Agent Anthropic Render
description: Level 8 vendor branch — Anthropic platform render format. Resolved from universal-render: capability_tier mapped to model name, capabilities exploded to tool-path pairs, custom output tool discovered, hooks built, frontmatter composed. 13 sections: 8 pass-through, 3 modified, 2 created. implicit_grants consumed during hook building.

identity.title: IdentityAnthropic
identity.description: Anthropic-resolved agent identity. Same as universal-render identity but capability_tier is replaced by the resolved model name. The tier is consumed during model resolution and does not appear in the output.

role_identity.title: RoleIdentity
role_identity.description:
Short noun phrase naming what this agent is. Not a sentence, not a role description — that belongs in role and capabilities. Examples: "semantic quality assessor", "interview summarizer", "embedding normalizer". This becomes the "You are a {identity}" opening in the generated prompt.
Natural language prose — must contain at least one whitespace character. Mutually exclusive with all identifier types. Used for descriptions, instructions, error messages, and display labels. Not a path.

x-semantic.intent: Establishes the agent's behavioral frame. The generated prompt opens "You are a {role_identity}" — vague identities produce vague behavior.
checks: Specific enough to distinguish this agent from others in the system
Noun phrase, not a sentence or role description
Names a recognizable specialist, not a generic label
anti_patterns: Sentences or descriptions instead of noun phrases

role_responsibility.title: RoleResponsibility
role_responsibility.description:
One-sentence mandate defining the agent's core obligation. This is the single most important thing the agent must accomplish. Everything else is secondary. Write as a direct imperative: "Assess each truth entry against quality dimensions and produce a structured QC report."
Substantive prose text that forms complete sentences. Starts with a capital letter, contains at least three whitespace characters, ends with sentence punctuation. Structural constraints prevent non-prose abuse, so path exclusions are not needed. Used for descriptions, instructions, and multi-sentence text that may reference file paths.

x-semantic.intent: Defines the agent's primary obligation. Everything else the agent does is secondary to this. A weak responsibility produces unfocused execution.
checks: Single clear mandate, not a list of duties
Written as direct imperative
Specific enough that completion is verifiable
Describes an outcome, not an activity
anti_patterns: Describing what the agent IS instead of what it MUST DO

role_description.title: RoleDescription
role_description.description:
Expanded role context that builds on role_identity and role_responsibility. Where identity says WHAT you are and responsibility says WHAT you must do, description provides the WHY and HOW — domain context, judgement guidance, and framing that shapes how the agent approaches its work. Optional for simple agents; increasingly valuable as task complexity and required judgement increase.
Substantive prose text that forms complete sentences. Starts with a capital letter, contains at least three whitespace characters, ends with sentence punctuation. Structural constraints prevent non-prose abuse, so path exclusions are not needed. Used for descriptions, instructions, and multi-sentence text that may reference file paths.

x-semantic.intent: Builds the agent's understanding of its role beyond the identity and responsibility. Provides context, nuance, and framing that helps the agent exercise good judgement in ambiguous situations.
checks: Adds context beyond what identity and responsibility already state
Helps the agent understand WHY it does what it does
Appropriate depth for task complexity — simple agents may omit entirely
anti_patterns: Restating role_identity or role_responsibility in different words
Generic filler: 'You are a helpful assistant that...'

items.title: RoleExpertiseItem
items.description:
Skill and knowledge areas the agent claims. Each entry is a concise phrase describing a competency relevant to the agent's task. These calibrate the LLM's self-model — declare expertise areas that directly support role_responsibility. Typical agents declare 2-5 entries. Be specific: "JSON Schema validation" not "validation", "Gothic linguistic terminology" not "languages". If provided, must contain at least one entry (omit the field entirely rather than providing an empty array). Entries must be unique.
Natural language prose — must contain at least one whitespace character. Mutually exclusive with all identifier types. Used for descriptions, instructions, error messages, and display labels. Not a path.

oneOf.title: SecurityBoundaryAnthropic
oneOf.description: Anthropic-resolved security boundary. Capabilities have been exploded to tool-path pairs and collapsed by workspace-relative path. Each display entry groups all tools and commands granted for a single path. Workspace_path has been extracted to critical_rules.

display.title: DisplayEntries
display.description: Security boundary display entries collapsed by workspace-relative path

items.title: DisplayEntry
items.description: A security boundary display entry grouping all tools and commands granted for a single workspace-relative path. Produced by exploding capabilities to tools and collapsing by path.

path.title: DisplayPath

oneOf.title: PathRelative
oneOf.description: Relative filesystem path starting with ./ — excludes traversal and sensitive path patterns. Workspace-relative, gets absolutized during resolution.

path.description:
Path in a security boundary display entry. Workspace-relative paths are produced by stripping the workspace root prefix from absolute grant paths (e.g., "./truth/", "./schemas/"). Paths outside the workspace remain absolute (e.g., "/tmp/bragi/").
Filesystem path — either relative (./) or absolute (/)

tools.title: DisplayToolsCommands
tools.description: Tool and command names granted for a specific workspace-relative path

items.title: DisplayToolCommand
items.description:
Tool or command name in a security boundary display entry. Can be a Claude Code tool name (Read, Grep, Glob, Write, Edit, Bash) or an allowed shell command (find, ls, du, wc, stat, diff, tree).
Either a Claude Code tool name (PascalCase: Read, Grep, Bash) or a shell command name (snake_case: find, ls, du, wc, stat, diff, tree).

security_boundary.description: Anthropic-resolved security boundary. Capabilities have been exploded to tool-path pairs and collapsed by workspace-relative path. Each display entry groups all tools and commands granted for a single path. Workspace_path has been extracted to critical_rules.

input.title: Input
input.description: What the agent receives: data format, delivery mechanism, schema for validation, parameters, and context resources. Context items use resolved variants (absolute paths).

delivery.title: DispatchInputDelivery
delivery.description:
How input data reaches the agent. 'file' means the agent reads from a pre- determined file path declared in the definition — also requires security_io_input_file in [security.security_io]. 'directory' means the agent reads from a pre-determined directory path — also requires security_io_input_directory in [security.security_io]. 'tempfile' means the dispatcher writes input to a scoped temp directory and passes the path as parameter — preserves context window for large inputs; also requires security_io_input_tempdir in [security.security_io]. 'inline' means embedded directly in the agent prompt (small inputs only, no file paths or security_io fields needed).
How input data reaches the agent. 'tempfile' means the dispatcher writes to a scoped temp directory and passes the path as parameter. 'inline' means embedded directly in the agent prompt. 'file' means the agent reads from a pre-determined file path. 'directory' means the agent reads from a pre-determined directory path.

input_schema.title: InputSchemaXAbs
input_schema.description:
Schema the input data validates against. Workspace-relative path to a .schema.json or .schema.yaml file. The resolver uses this for input validation enforcement — a security property.
Absolute path that must exist on the filesystem

context.title: ContextResources
context.description: Context resources available to the agent — required items that must be provided and optional items available on request.

context_required.title: ContextRequired
context_required.description: Required context resources — paths absolutized after resolution

context_available.title: ContextAvailable
context_available.description: Available context resources — paths absolutized after resolution

output.title: Output
output.description: What the agent produces: format, file location, naming rules, and optional schema for validation. Aggregates fields from task.processing, security.security_schema, and security.security_io.

description.title: OutputDescription
description.description:
Human-readable description of the output data the agent produces. Describes what the output contains and its downstream purpose. The mechanical format is captured by processing_output_file_format — this field captures domain meaning, but repeating format for human readability is acceptable. Example: "One assessment record per input entry with quality scores and failure annotations"
Natural language prose — must contain at least one whitespace character. Mutually exclusive with all identifier types. Used for descriptions, instructions, error messages, and display labels. Not a path.

name_known.title: NameKnown
name_known.description:
How well the output filename is known at definition time. known: exact output file path is declared — also requires security_io_output_file in [security.security_io]. partially: a naming template or instruction constrains the filename but the LLM provides variable parts — also requires security_io_output_directory in [security.security_io], plus processing_output_file_name_template. unknown: completely dynamic, no naming constraint — also requires security_io_output_directory in [security.security_io], plus processing_output_file_name_instruction.
How well the output filename is known at definition time. 'known' means exact path is declared. 'partially' means a naming template constrains the filename. 'unknown' means completely dynamic naming.

schema_path.title: SchemaPathXAbs
schema_path.description:
Path to the JSON Schema file that validates enforcement tool output. Required for all enforcement output tools — structured output (JSON, JSONL) always requires schema validation. The tool validates each write against this schema before committing to disk.
Absolute path that must exist on the filesystem

schema_embed.title: SchemaEmbed
schema_embed.description:
Whether to embed the output schema directly into the agent prompt. When true, the format transformer reads the schema file and inlines its content — uses context window but ensures the agent sees the schema without a tool call. When false (or omitted), the schema path is granted read access and the agent reads it via Read tool — saves context but adds a tool-call round trip. Prefer true for small schemas (under ~100 lines) or when schema adherence is critical. Prefer false for large schemas where context window conservation matters. Either way the agent knows the desired shape.
True or false value

output_file.title: OutputFileAbs
output_file.description:
Absolute path to the specific file the agent writes its output to. Used in the render schema to specify the resolved output location when the agent produces a single file with a known name.
Absolute filesystem path starting with / — excludes traversal and sensitive path patterns. The resolved form after absolutization.

output_directory.title: OutputDirectoryAbs
output_directory.description:
Absolute path to the directory where the agent writes output files. Used in the render schema to specify the resolved output location when the agent produces multiple files or when file names are partially or fully unknown.
Absolute filesystem path starting with / — excludes traversal and sensitive path patterns. The resolved form after absolutization.

name_template.title: NameTemplate
name_template.description:
Filename template with {placeholder} syntax for dispatch-time parameters. The tool constructs the output filename by substituting placeholder values provided by the LLM (received as dispatch parameters). The tool controls directory, naming pattern, and extension. The LLM controls only the variable parts. Example: "{interview-id}.summaries.jsonl" — the LLM provides interview-id, the tool constructs the full path.
Filename template with a {variable} placeholder and file extension. The variable becomes the --name CLI argument for the output tool. The extension segments determine the output file suffix. LLM authors write the complete template; the build system decomposes it into tool arguments and write paths.

name_instruction.title: NameInstruction
name_instruction.description:
Instruction indicating what the LLM should use as the filename basis during processing. The LLM derives the identifier from the data being processed. The tool writes to output_directory/{identifier}.{extension}, where the extension is enforced by processing_output_file_format. The LLM controls the filename but not the directory or file type. Example: "{record-identifier}" — the LLM provides a record identifier, the tool writes to the output directory with the correct extension.
Substantive prose text that forms complete sentences. Starts with a capital letter, contains at least three whitespace characters, ends with sentence punctuation. Structural constraints prevent non-prose abuse, so path exclusions are not needed. Used for descriptions, instructions, and multi-sentence text that may reference file paths.

oneOf.title: WritingOutputAnthropic
oneOf.description: Anthropic-resolved output tool specification. The raw enforcement fields have been matched against the custom tool lookup table to produce a resolved tool name and invocation pattern. Null when no custom tool exists for this agent.

invocation_variant.title: InvocationVariant
invocation_variant.description:
How the custom tool is invoked. no-name: output path is fully known, the tool takes data on stdin and writes to a fixed path. with-name: the agent generates a filename from a pattern or instruction before each invocation.
Custom tool invocation variants. Determines whether the agent must generate a filename before invoking the output tool. no-name: output path is fully known, tool takes data only. with-name: agent generates a filename from a pattern or instruction before invocation.

invocation_display.title: InvocationDisplay
invocation_display.description:
Ready-to-use bash heredoc showing the exact invocation pattern for the custom output tool. Composed during anthropic render from the resolved tool name, schema path, and output path. Displayed in the writing_output section of the generated prompt.
Natural language prose — must contain at least one whitespace character. Mutually exclusive with all identifier types. Used for descriptions, instructions, error messages, and display labels. Not a path.

name_pattern.title: OutputToolNamePattern
name_pattern.description:
Naming pattern constraint for LLM-provided filenames. Only present when the output filename is partially known — the definition provides a template or instruction and the LLM fills in the variable parts. The tool enforces this pattern when constructing the output path.
Filename template with a {variable} placeholder and file extension. The variable becomes the --name CLI argument for the output tool. The extension segments determine the output file suffix. LLM authors write the complete template; the build system decomposes it into tool arguments and write paths.

schema_path.title: OutputToolSchemaXAbs
schema_path.description:
Path to the JSON Schema file that validates enforcement tool output. Required for all enforcement output tools — structured output (JSON, JSONL) always requires schema validation. The tool validates each write against this schema before committing to disk.
Absolute path to a JSON Schema file that must exist on the filesystem

file_path.title: OutputToolFilePathAbs
file_path.description:
Resolved absolute path to the output file. Present when the output filename is fully known at definition time. The enforcement tool writes exclusively to this path.
Absolute filesystem path starting with / — excludes traversal and sensitive path patterns. The resolved form after absolutization.

directory_path.title: OutputToolDirectoryPathAbs
directory_path.description:
Resolved absolute path to the output directory. Present when the output filename is not fully known at definition time. The enforcement tool writes files within this directory, with filenames constrained by enforcement_output_tool_name_pattern when available.
Absolute filesystem path starting with / — excludes traversal and sensitive path patterns. The resolved form after absolutization.

writing_output.description: Anthropic-resolved output tool specification. The raw enforcement fields have been matched against the custom tool lookup table to produce a resolved tool name and invocation pattern. Null when no custom tool exists for this agent.

oneOf.title: Constraints
oneOf.description: Behavioral constraint rules the agent must follow. Null when no constraints defined.

rules.title: GuardrailsConstraints
rules.description: MUST and NEVER rules the agent must follow. Each entry is a single imperative constraint. Keep constraints specific and verifiable.

items.title: GuardrailsConstraint
items.description:
MUST and NEVER rules the agent must follow. Each entry is a single imperative constraint. "MUST validate every record against schema before writing", "NEVER modify source data", "MUST process records in order". Keep constraints specific and verifiable — vague rules get ignored.
Substantive prose text that forms complete sentences. Starts with a capital letter, contains at least three whitespace characters, ends with sentence punctuation. Structural constraints prevent non-prose abuse, so path exclusions are not needed. Used for descriptions, instructions, and multi-sentence text that may reference file paths.

x-semantic.intent: Hard behavioral boundaries in the agent prompt. Violations are agent failures. Each item must be clear enough that both the agent AND a reviewer can determine whether a specific output violates it.
checks: Each item is actionable — agent can determine compliance from the constraint alone
Each item is verifiable — a reviewer can check violation without ambiguity
Items are specific to this agent's failure modes, not generic good practice
anti_patterns: Constraints the agent cannot actually verify or enforce

constraints.description: Behavioral constraint rules the agent must follow. Null when no constraints defined.

oneOf.title: AntiPatterns
oneOf.description: Known failure patterns the agent must avoid. Null when no anti-patterns defined.

patterns.title: GuardrailsAntiPatterns
patterns.description: Common mistakes to avoid. Each entry describes a specific wrong behavior the agent might exhibit and why it's wrong.

items.title: GuardrailsAntiPattern
items.description:
Common mistakes to avoid. Each entry describes a specific wrong behavior the agent might exhibit and why it's wrong. "Do not batch-summarize from memory — process each record individually from the source file", "Do not infer missing fields — mark them as absent". Anti-patterns are learned from observed agent failures.
Substantive prose text that forms complete sentences. Starts with a capital letter, contains at least three whitespace characters, ends with sentence punctuation. Structural constraints prevent non-prose abuse, so path exclusions are not needed. Used for descriptions, instructions, and multi-sentence text that may reference file paths.

x-semantic.intent: Calibrates the LLM against its own failure modes. Each item must describe a specific, recognizable mistake — not a generic warning.
checks: Each item describes a specific mistake, not a category of mistakes
Each item is recognizable — agent can detect when it is about to do this
Items are grounded in observed LLM failure modes, not hypothetical risks

anti_patterns.description: Known failure patterns the agent must avoid. Null when no anti-patterns defined.

return_format.title: ReturnFormat
return_format.description: How the agent reports results: return mode, optional instructions for status/metrics/output, schema for structured returns, and success/failure criteria. Aggregates from task.return and criteria sections.

status_instruction.title: StatusInstruction
status_instruction.description:
Prompt instruction telling the agent how to report its completion status in its return. Composed into the agent prompt when return mode includes status. Example: "Return only SUCCESS or FAILURE."
Substantive prose text that forms complete sentences. Starts with a capital letter, contains at least three whitespace characters, ends with sentence punctuation. Structural constraints prevent non-prose abuse, so path exclusions are not needed. Used for descriptions, instructions, and multi-sentence text that may reference file paths.

metrics_instruction.title: MetricsInstruction
metrics_instruction.description:
Prompt instruction telling the agent how to report summary metrics in its return. Composed into the agent prompt when return mode includes metrics. Example: "Include summary metrics with your return: records processed, records passed, records failed."
Substantive prose text that forms complete sentences. Starts with a capital letter, contains at least three whitespace characters, ends with sentence punctuation. Structural constraints prevent non-prose abuse, so path exclusions are not needed. Used for descriptions, instructions, and multi-sentence text that may reference file paths.

output_instruction.title: OutputInstruction
output_instruction.description:
Prompt instruction telling the agent how to deliver its output data in its return. Composed into the agent prompt when return mode includes output. Example: "Return your output directly as your final message to the dispatcher."
Substantive prose text that forms complete sentences. Starts with a capital letter, contains at least three whitespace characters, ends with sentence punctuation. Structural constraints prevent non-prose abuse, so path exclusions are not needed. Used for descriptions, instructions, and multi-sentence text that may reference file paths.

return_schema.title: ReturnSchemaXAbs
return_schema.description:
Absolute path to a JSON Schema file (must end with .schema.json or .schema.yaml) defining the metric fields the agent returns. Always embedded directly into the prompt — there is no enforcement mechanism for return communication (agent-to-dispatcher LLM text). Embedding ensures the agent sees field names, types, and definitions. Schema file must exist at resolution time. Example: "definitions/schemas/my-agent-return.schema.json"
Absolute path that must exist on the filesystem

success_criteria.title: SuccessCriteria
success_criteria.description: Success criteria — includes inlined, direct items only

items.title: SuccessItem
items.description: A single success criterion with definition and observable evidence

success_definition.title: SuccessDefinition
success_definition.description:
One-sentence statement of what success means for this agent. LLMs are goal- driven — explicit success definitions pull harder than constraints. Write as a positive outcome: "Every input record has been assessed and a valid QC report written to disk."
Substantive prose text that forms complete sentences. Starts with a capital letter, contains at least three whitespace characters, ends with sentence punctuation. Structural constraints prevent non-prose abuse, so path exclusions are not needed. Used for descriptions, instructions, and multi-sentence text that may reference file paths.

x-semantic.intent: The agent's goal state. LLMs are goal-driven — explicit success definitions pull behavior more effectively than constraints push it.
checks: Describes a concrete end state, not an ongoing activity
Refers to the PROCESS succeeding, not data quality outcomes
Observable — you can tell from examining outputs whether this was achieved
anti_patterns: Confusing process success with data quality ('all entries are high quality' is data, not process)
Vague outcomes: 'task completed successfully', 'all items processed'

success_evidence.title: SuccessEvidence
success_evidence.description: Observable evidence that a success criterion has been met

items.title: SuccessEvidenceItem
items.description:
Observable conditions that prove success. Each entry is a concrete, verifiable statement the agent can check. "Output record count equals input record count", "Every record passes schema validation". These become the agent's self-verification checklist.
Substantive prose text that forms complete sentences. Starts with a capital letter, contains at least three whitespace characters, ends with sentence punctuation. Structural constraints prevent non-prose abuse, so path exclusions are not needed. Used for descriptions, instructions, and multi-sentence text that may reference file paths.

x-semantic.intent: Self-verification checklist. The agent checks each condition after processing to confirm success before reporting.
checks: Each item is a concrete, observable condition — not a subjective judgment
Each item is independently verifiable from outputs alone
Conditions are sufficient — if all pass, success is confirmed

failure_criteria.title: FailureCriteria
failure_criteria.description: Failure criteria — includes inlined, direct items only

items.title: FailureItem
items.description: A single failure criterion — FAILURE means process broke, not data quality

failure_definition.title: FailureDefinition
failure_definition.description:
One-sentence statement of what failure means for this agent. Failure refers to the PROCESS, not the DATA. An agent that correctly identifies all inputs as invalid has SUCCEEDED — the assessment process worked. FAILURE means the process itself broke: couldn't read input, couldn't write output, unrecoverable error.
Substantive prose text that forms complete sentences. Starts with a capital letter, contains at least three whitespace characters, ends with sentence punctuation. Structural constraints prevent non-prose abuse, so path exclusions are not needed. Used for descriptions, instructions, and multi-sentence text that may reference file paths.

x-semantic.intent: Defines process failure — not data outcomes. The agent uses this to determine when to report FAILURE vs SUCCESS with bad-data findings.
checks: Describes PROCESS failure, not data quality problems
Specific failure conditions, not 'something went wrong'
Distinguishable from success_definition — no overlap
anti_patterns: Treating bad data as failure ('found invalid entries' is SUCCESS if the process worked)

failure_evidence.title: FailureEvidence
failure_evidence.description: Observable evidence that a failure criterion has been triggered

items.title: FailureEvidenceItem
items.description:
Observable conditions that prove failure. Each entry is a concrete condition indicating the process broke. "Any record skipped without explanation", "Schema validation failure not resolved after retry", "Output file not created". These are process failures, not data quality findings.
Substantive prose text that forms complete sentences. Starts with a capital letter, contains at least three whitespace characters, ends with sentence punctuation. Structural constraints prevent non-prose abuse, so path exclusions are not needed. Used for descriptions, instructions, and multi-sentence text that may reference file paths.

x-semantic.intent: Process failure detection. The agent checks these conditions to determine whether to report FAILURE instead of SUCCESS.
checks: Each item describes a PROCESS failure condition, not a data quality finding
Each item is observable from the execution environment
Conditions are distinct from success_evidence — no overlap

dispatcher.title: Dispatcher
dispatcher.description: Everything the dispatcher skill needs to launch and feed the agent: identity, mode, batching, input/output format, parameters.

agent_name.title: AgentName
agent_name.description:
Kebab-case identifier for the agent. Becomes the frontmatter `name` field in the generated agent prompt. Must be unique across all agent definitions. Use descriptive names that communicate domain and function: truth-system- quality-control, not qc-agent.
Lowercase kebab-case string — words separated by hyphens. Used for identifiers that must be URL-safe and filesystem-safe.

dispatch_mode.title: DispatchMode
dispatch_mode.description:
How the dispatcher feeds work to the agent. 'batch' means the dispatcher splits input into chunks and invokes the agent once per chunk — requires dispatch_batch_size. 'full' means the dispatcher passes all input at once in a single agent invocation.
How the dispatcher feeds work to the agent. 'batch' splits input into chunks and invokes the agent once per chunk — requires dispatch_batch_size. 'full' passes all input at once in a single agent invocation.

background_mode.title: DispatchBackgroundMode
background_mode.description:
Background execution policy for this agent. Determines how the dispatcher handles this agent's execution lifecycle. 'allowed' means the dispatcher chooses foreground or background based on workload — most common choice. 'required' means the dispatcher must launch this agent as a background process — use for long-running agents that should not block the dispatcher. 'forbidden' means the agent must run in the foreground and the dispatcher waits for completion — use for interactive agents requiring user input.
Background execution policy. 'allowed' means the dispatcher chooses foreground or background based on workload. 'required' means the agent must run as a background process. 'forbidden' means the agent must run in the foreground and the dispatcher waits for completion.

input_delivery.title: InputDelivery
input_delivery.description:
How input data reaches the agent. 'file' means the agent reads from a pre- determined file path declared in the definition — also requires security_io_input_file in [security.security_io]. 'directory' means the agent reads from a pre-determined directory path — also requires security_io_input_directory in [security.security_io]. 'tempfile' means the dispatcher writes input to a scoped temp directory and passes the path as parameter — preserves context window for large inputs; also requires security_io_input_tempdir in [security.security_io]. 'inline' means embedded directly in the agent prompt (small inputs only, no file paths or security_io fields needed).
How input data reaches the agent. 'tempfile' means the dispatcher writes to a scoped temp directory and passes the path as parameter. 'inline' means embedded directly in the agent prompt. 'file' means the agent reads from a pre-determined file path. 'directory' means the agent reads from a pre-determined directory path.

output_name_known.title: OutputNameKnown
output_name_known.description:
How well the output filename is known at definition time. known: exact output file path is declared — also requires security_io_output_file in [security.security_io]. partially: a naming template or instruction constrains the filename but the LLM provides variable parts — also requires security_io_output_directory in [security.security_io], plus processing_output_file_name_template. unknown: completely dynamic, no naming constraint — also requires security_io_output_directory in [security.security_io], plus processing_output_file_name_instruction.
How well the output filename is known at definition time. 'known' means exact path is declared. 'partially' means a naming template constrains the filename. 'unknown' means completely dynamic naming.

max_agents.title: DispatchMaxAgents
max_agents.description:
Maximum number of concurrent agent instances the dispatcher may spawn. Controls parallelism for batch processing. The dispatcher launches up to this many agents simultaneously, each processing a different chunk. Defaults to 6 if not specified.
Whole number value

batch_size.title: DispatchBatchSize
batch_size.description:
Tuple of [min, max] records per batch chunk. The dispatcher splits input into chunks of size between min and max. Min must be strictly less than max. Required when dispatch_mode is 'batch'. Example: [50, 100] means each agent invocation gets between 50 and 100 records.
[min, max] records per batch chunk. Min must be strictly less than max. The dispatcher splits input into chunks of size between min and max.

instructions.title: Instructions
instructions.description: Ordered processing steps — includes inlined, for render consumption

steps.title: ExecutionInstructions
steps.description: Ordered processing steps — includes inlined, direct steps only

items.title: InstructionStep
items.description: Inline instruction step with processing mode boundary

instruction_mode.title: InstructionMode
instruction_mode.description:
Processing mode boundary. DETERMINISTIC steps are mechanical operations (reading input, writing output, validating schema) where the LLM must follow exact procedures with no creativity. PROBABILISTIC steps require LLM intelligence (rewriting text, making quality judgments, creative decisions). The transformer uses mode declarations to compile different prompt patterns for each step type.
Processing mode boundary. 'deterministic' steps are mechanical operations where the LLM must follow exact procedures. 'probabilistic' steps require LLM intelligence for creative or evaluative work.

instruction_text.title: InstructionText
instruction_text.description:
Inline instruction text for this step. Used for short instructions that don't warrant a separate .md file. Mutually exclusive with include.
Markdown-formatted text content. Starts with a non-path character, contains at least three whitespace characters. No path exclusions needed — the structural constraints prevent abuse while allowing markdown formatting and embedded path references. Used for example content, instructional text, and rich-text fields.

x-semantic.intent: Directs agent behavior for one processing step. Each instruction must produce consistent behavior across different LLM instances.
checks: Specific enough that two different LLMs would produce similar outputs
Describes concrete actions, not aspirational goals
Scoped to a single processing step, not the entire task

oneOf.title: Examples
oneOf.description: Example groups — includes inlined, for render consumption

groups.title: ExecutionExamples
groups.description: Example groups — includes inlined, direct groups only

items.title: ExampleGroup
items.description: A named group of calibration examples — includes inlined, direct entries only

example_group_name.title: ExampleGroupName
example_group_name.description:
Name of the example group, used as the H3 heading when compiling examples into the agent prompt. Groups organize examples by what they demonstrate — "correct rewrite", "incorrect compression", "edge cases".
Title Case string — each word starts uppercase, separated by spaces. Used for display titles, section headings, and short labels. Not prose (no sentences), not an identifier (has spaces).

example_display_headings.title: ExampleDisplayHeadings
example_display_headings.description:
Toggle per-group display of individual example headings. When false, examples render as items under the group H3. When true, each example gets its own H4 heading derived from the H2 in the resolved content. Controls detail level without changing content.
True or false value

examples_max_number.title: ExamplesMaxNumber
examples_max_number.description:
Maximum number of examples to include from this group after include resolution and H2 splitting. Applied AFTER the transformer resolves @include references and splits on H2 boundaries — the count is about resolved individual examples, not raw array entries. Omit to include all examples in the group.
Whole number value

example_entries.title: ExampleEntries
example_entries.description: Example entries — includes inlined, direct entries only

items.title: ExampleEntry
items.description: Inline example with heading and text content

example_heading.title: ExampleHeading
example_heading.description:
Heading for an individual example entry. When example_display_headings is true, this becomes the H4 heading for the example in the generated prompt. When derived from @include, the resolver extracts this from the H2 heading in the source .md file.
Natural language prose — must contain at least one whitespace character. Mutually exclusive with all identifier types. Used for descriptions, instructions, error messages, and display labels. Not a path.

example_text.title: ExampleText
example_text.description:
Inline example text for this entry. Used for short examples that don't warrant a separate .md file. Mutually exclusive with include.
Markdown-formatted text content. Starts with a non-path character, contains at least three whitespace characters. No path exclusions needed — the structural constraints prevent abuse while allowing markdown formatting and embedded path references. Used for example content, instructional text, and rich-text fields.

examples.description: Example groups — includes inlined, for render consumption

critical_rules.title: CriticalRules
critical_rules.description: End-of-lifecycle fields duplicated for self-contained template consumption. Workspace path extracted from security_boundary. Tool summary fields duplicated from resolved writing_output. These fields are fully resolved and will not change again.

workspace_path.title: WorkspacePathXAbs
workspace_path.description:
Absolute filesystem path to the workspace root directory. All workspace- relative paths in the definition (context paths, schema paths, allowed_read/write paths) are resolved relative to this directory. Must be an absolute path (starting with /). Validated against the blocklist during resolution. Any path that resolves outside this workspace or into a blocked zone triggers a SecurityIncident. Example: "/Users/username/.ai/spaces/myproject"
Absolute path that must exist on the filesystem

has_output_tool.title: HasOutputTool
has_output_tool.description:
Whether this agent has a custom output tool for writing structured output. When true, the agent must use the resolved tool for all output writes. When false, the agent uses standard Write or Edit tools directly.
True or false value

frontmatter.title: Frontmatter
frontmatter.description: Agent metadata for the TOML frontmatter header of the generated prompt file. Composed from identity, resolved model, exploded tool grants, and fully resolved hook configuration. The hooks container carries the complete Claude Code hook configuration for path enforcement.

permission_mode.title: PermissionMode
permission_mode.description:
Claude Code permission mode for agent execution. bypassPermissions means the agent runs without interactive permission prompts, relying entirely on PreToolUse hooks for path and command enforcement.
Claude Code permission modes for agent execution. bypassPermissions: agent runs with hooks-based enforcement instead of interactive permission prompts. All tool access is controlled by PreToolUse hooks that validate paths and commands.

tools.title: FrontmatterTools
tools.description: All Claude Code tool names granted to this agent. Each item is a PascalCase tool name. Composed at render time into the comma-separated frontmatter tools field.

items.title: FrontmatterTool
items.description:
A single Claude Code tool name granted to this agent. PascalCase identifier matching the Claude Code tool naming convention. Examples: Bash, Edit, Glob, Grep, Read, Write.
PascalCase string — starts uppercase, word boundaries marked by uppercase letters. Used for tool names and type identifiers that follow PascalCase convention (e.g., Bash, Read, PreToolUse).

hooks.title: HooksConfig
hooks.description: Hook enforcement data for the agent. Stores what tools, commands, and output tools are granted — pure data with no rendering concerns. Galdr composes this into Claude Code PreToolUse hook CLI commands at render time.

output_tool.title: OutputToolName
output_tool.description:
Name of the resolved output tool binary. Produced by matching the enforcement output tool specification against the tool registry during anthropic render. Example: write_truth_entry.
Lowercase snake_case string — words separated by underscores. Used for parameter names and template placeholders.

tool_entries.title: ToolPathEntries
tool_entries.description: Claude Code tools with their granted path prefixes. One entry per tool.

items.title: ToolPathEntry
items.description: A Claude Code tool with its granted path prefixes. Each entry binds one Anthropic tool to the absolute paths it may access. At render time, entries are composed into hook enforcement CLI arguments.

tool.title: ToolNameAnthropic
tool.description:
Claude Code tool name for the Anthropic platform. One of: Read, Grep, Glob, Write, Edit, Bash.
Claude Code tool names for the Anthropic platform. Each value is a tool that Claude Code exposes and that hook enforcement validates against. Read: file read. Grep/Glob: content/file search. Write: file create/overwrite. Edit: targeted file modification. Bash: shell command execution.

command_entries.title: CommandPathEntries
command_entries.description: Unix commands with their granted path prefixes. One entry per command.

items.title: CommandPathEntry
items.description: A Unix command with its granted path prefixes. Each entry binds one shell command to the absolute paths it may inspect. At render time, entries are composed into hook enforcement CLI arguments.

command.title: CommandNameUnix
command.description:
Unix shell command name. One of: find, ls, du, wc, stat, diff, tree.
Unix commands granted to agents for filesystem inspection. find: locate files by name. ls: list directory contents. du: disk usage. wc: word/line count. stat: file metadata. diff: file comparison. tree: directory tree.

atom__title_string.title: TitleString
atom__title_string.description: Title Case string — each word starts uppercase, separated by spaces. Used for display titles, section headings, and short labels. Not prose (no sentences), not an identifier (has spaces).

field__agent_title.title: AgentTitle
field__agent_title.description:
Human-readable agent title derived mechanically from agent_name. Split on hyphens, capitalize each word. Becomes the frontmatter title field in the generated agent prompt.
Title Case string — each word starts uppercase, separated by spaces. Used for display titles, section headings, and short labels. Not prose (no sentences), not an identifier (has spaces).

atom__string_prose.title: StringProse
atom__string_prose.description: Substantive prose text that forms complete sentences. Starts with a capital letter, contains at least three whitespace characters, ends with sentence punctuation. Structural constraints prevent non-prose abuse, so path exclusions are not needed. Used for descriptions, instructions, and multi-sentence text that may reference file paths.

field__agent_description.title: AgentDescription
field__agent_description.description:
One-line purpose statement for the agent. Becomes the frontmatter `description` field in the generated agent prompt. Should complete the sentence "This agent..." without starting with "This agent". Be specific about what the agent does, not what it is. "Assesses truth entries against quality dimensions" not "A quality control agent".
Substantive prose text that forms complete sentences. Starts with a capital letter, contains at least three whitespace characters, ends with sentence punctuation. Structural constraints prevent non-prose abuse, so path exclusions are not needed. Used for descriptions, instructions, and multi-sentence text that may reference file paths.

x-semantic.intent: Communicates the agent's purpose to humans and systems that select agents for tasks. Vague descriptions make agents undiscoverable.
checks: Completes the sentence 'This agent...' naturally
Describes what the agent does, not what it is
Specific enough to distinguish from other agents
anti_patterns: Starting with 'This agent' or 'An agent that'
Describing identity instead of action: 'A quality control agent'

atom__string_text.title: StringText
atom__string_text.description: Natural language prose — must contain at least one whitespace character. Mutually exclusive with all identifier types. Used for descriptions, instructions, error messages, and display labels. Not a path.

field__anthropic_model.title: AnthropicModel
field__anthropic_model.description:
Resolved Anthropic model name for this agent. Produced by mapping the platform-agnostic capability_tier to a concrete model at the anthropic render stage. haiku for fast-cheap, sonnet for standard and analytical, opus for complex-reasoning and max-capability, inherit to match the dispatcher.
Resolved Anthropic model names. The anthropic render stage maps the platform-agnostic capability_tier to a concrete Anthropic model. haiku: fast/cheap tasks. sonnet: standard and analytical tasks. opus: complex reasoning and max capability. inherit: match the dispatcher's model.

atom__path_absolute.title: PathAbsolute
atom__path_absolute.description: Absolute filesystem path starting with / — excludes traversal and sensitive path patterns. The resolved form after absolutization.

atom__pascal_string.title: PascalString
atom__pascal_string.description: PascalCase string — starts uppercase, word boundaries marked by uppercase letters. Used for tool names and type identifiers that follow PascalCase convention (e.g., Bash, Read, PreToolUse).

atom__snake_string.title: SnakeString
atom__snake_string.description: Lowercase snake_case string — words separated by underscores. Used for parameter names and template placeholders.

field__input_description.title: InputDescription
field__input_description.description:
Human-readable description of the input data the agent receives. Describes what the records represent and what the agent does with them. The mechanical format is captured by dispatch_input_format and delivery by dispatch_input_delivery — this field captures domain meaning, but repeating format for human readability is acceptable. Example: "Embedding target records to rewrite and compress to 80-150 characters"
Natural language prose — must contain at least one whitespace character. Mutually exclusive with all identifier types. Used for descriptions, instructions, error messages, and display labels. Not a path.

field__dispatch_input_format.title: DispatchInputFormat
field__dispatch_input_format.description:
Format of the input data the agent receives. 'jsonl' for newline-delimited JSON records (one per line). 'json' for a single JSON document. 'text' for unstructured text content. This determines how the agent should parse the input file delivered via the delivery mechanism.
Format of input file content. 'jsonl' for newline-delimited JSON records, 'json' for a single JSON document, 'text' for unstructured text.

enum__dispatch_input_delivery.title: DispatchInputDelivery
enum__dispatch_input_delivery.description: How input data reaches the agent. 'tempfile' means the dispatcher writes to a scoped temp directory and passes the path as parameter. 'inline' means embedded directly in the agent prompt. 'file' means the agent reads from a pre-determined file path. 'directory' means the agent reads from a pre-determined directory path.

element__path_exists_absolute.title: PathExistsAbsolute
element__path_exists_absolute.description: Absolute path that must exist on the filesystem

array__dispatch_parameters.title: DispatchParameters
array__dispatch_parameters.description: Named parameters the dispatcher passes to the agent at invocation

items.title: ParameterItem
items.description: A parameter the dispatcher passes to the agent at invocation

param_name.title: ParamName
param_name.description:
Name of a parameter the dispatcher passes to the agent. This becomes the placeholder name in the agent prompt template. Common names: 'tempfile' (path to input data), 'uid' (record identifier), 'iteration' (processing round number).
Lowercase snake_case string — words separated by underscores. Used for parameter names and template placeholders.

param_type.title: ParamType
param_type.description:
Type of the parameter value. Used for documentation and dispatcher validation. 'path' for filesystem paths, 'string' for arbitrary text, 'integer' for numeric values, 'boolean' for true/false flags.
Type of a dispatch parameter value. Used for documentation and dispatcher validation.

param_required.title: ParamRequired
param_required.description:
Whether this parameter must be provided by the dispatcher. Required parameters cause dispatcher failure if missing. Optional parameters have sensible defaults or conditional behavior.
True or false value

param_description.title: ParamDescription
param_description.description:
Human-readable description of what a dispatcher parameter represents and how the agent should interpret it. Optional — parameter name and type may be sufficient for self-documenting parameters.
Natural language prose — must contain at least one whitespace character. Mutually exclusive with all identifier types. Used for descriptions, instructions, error messages, and display labels. Not a path.

simplegroup__context_item.title: ContextItem
simplegroup__context_item.description: A label+path pair for a context resource — paths absolutized after resolution

context_label.title: ContextLabel
context_label.description:
Display label for a context resource. Used in the generated prompt to create readable section headers. "Output Schema", "Canonical Glossary", "Operations Guide". Keep concise — this appears in the agent's prompt.
Title Case string — each word starts uppercase, separated by spaces. Used for display titles, section headings, and short labels. Not prose (no sentences), not an identifier (has spaces).

x-semantic.intent: Human-readable label that identifies a context resource in the agent prompt. Must be meaningful enough to distinguish resources from each other.
checks: Descriptive enough to identify the resource without seeing its content
Concise — a label, not a sentence

context_path.title: ContextPathAbs
context_path.description:
Workspace-relative path to a context resource. The transformer uses this to both generate prompt sections (telling the agent about the resource) AND add the path to read hooks (granting access). This dual-purpose mechanism ensures prompt awareness and permission always stay in sync.
Absolute filesystem path starting with / — excludes traversal and sensitive path patterns. The resolved form after absolutization.

field__output_format_kind.title: OutputFormatKind
field__output_format_kind.description:
Output format the agent produces. Choose based on output structure: 'jsonl' for record-oriented output where each line is an independent JSON object (supports per-record and batch write frequency control). 'json' for a single structured JSON document. 'markdown' for prose or structured text with headings. 'text' for unstructured plain text. Format transformers use this to add enforcement (e.g., hooks that verify valid JSONL before allowing writes).
Output format the agent produces. 'jsonl' for record-oriented output, 'json' for a single structured document, 'markdown' for prose or structured text with headings, 'text' for unstructured plain text.

enum__output_name_known.title: OutputNameKnown
enum__output_name_known.description: How well the output filename is known at definition time. 'known' means exact path is declared. 'partially' means a naming template constrains the filename. 'unknown' means completely dynamic naming.

atom__filename_template.title: FilenameTemplate
atom__filename_template.description: Filename template with a {variable} placeholder and file extension. The variable becomes the --name CLI argument for the output tool. The extension segments determine the output file suffix. LLM authors write the complete template; the build system decomposes it into tool arguments and write paths.

field__tool_name.title: ToolName
field__tool_name.description:
Resolved name of the custom output tool. Produced by matching the enforcement output tool specification against the custom tool lookup table during anthropic render. Example: "append_validated_jsonl_batch.py".
Lowercase snake_case string — words separated by underscores. Used for parameter names and template placeholders.

field__output_tool_name_needed.title: OutputToolNameNeeded
field__output_tool_name_needed.description:
Whether the LLM must provide a filename when invoking the output tool. Only present when the output filename is not fully known at definition time. When true, the LLM provides a name or identifier that the tool uses to construct the output path within the output directory.
True or false value

field__output_tool_batch_size.title: OutputToolBatchSize
field__output_tool_batch_size.description:
Number of records per write tool call when write frequency is batch. The agent accumulates this many records before invoking the write tool. Balances write frequency against data loss risk from interruption.
Whole number value

field__return_mode.title: ReturnMode
field__return_mode.description:
How the agent returns results to the dispatcher. status: return only SUCCESS or FAILURE. status-metrics: return status plus summary metrics. metrics- output: return metrics plus actual output data. output: return output directly, no status word needed. Determines which return instructions the format transformer composes into the prompt.
How the agent returns results. 'status' returns only SUCCESS or FAILURE. 'status-metrics' returns status plus summary metrics. 'metrics-output' returns metrics plus actual output data. 'output' returns output directly with no status word.

atom__string_markdown.title: StringMarkdown
atom__string_markdown.description: Markdown-formatted text content. Starts with a non-path character, contains at least three whitespace characters. No path exclusions needed — the structural constraints prevent abuse while allowing markdown formatting and embedded path references. Used for example content, instructional text, and rich-text fields.

simplearray__path_prefixes.title: PathPrefixes
simplearray__path_prefixes.description: Absolute path prefixes granted for access scoping. Each prefix authorizes access to any path that starts with it.

items.title: PathPrefix
items.description:
Absolute filesystem path prefix used for access scoping. Tools and commands granted this prefix can access any path that starts with it.
Absolute filesystem path starting with / — excludes traversal and sensitive path patterns. The resolved form after absolutization.
